headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can feed instructions or data into ComfyUI, but ComfyUI is offline and file-limited, so the pair mainly risks prompt injection and workflow errors rather than direct exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate external content and broad network egress, while ComfyUI accepts workflows and files in an asynchronous queue. If Airflow passes untrusted text or generated prompts into ComfyUI, the content can steer downstream behavior. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airflow forwards untrusted prompt text or workflow JSON into ComfyUI
IF a shared filesystem or API bridge is configured between the two
mitigations: Validate and sanitize all Airflow-to-ComfyUI payloads
Use a fixed schema for workflow inputs
Add allowlists for prompt fields and node types
Separate orchestration and generation into different service accounts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every queued job

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow touches no declared sensitive data classes, and ComfyUI is documented as offline with vendor-only egress. There is no shared filesystem or authenticated principal shown, so a direct leakage path is not evidenced. The main residual risk is accidental inclusion of sensitive inputs in Airflow tasks, which is limited by the current profiles.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks are configured to pass sensitive files into ComfyUI
IF operators mount a shared workspace containing secrets
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of the shared job inputs
Run both agents under separate OS users
Disable any shared mount that contains secrets
Review Airflow task templates for embedded credentials
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before queue submission

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while ComfyUI cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible overlap is shared external API usage or a shared queue, which is not documented here, so the conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API or queue
IF an operator adds a shared writable directory
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials per agent
Avoid shared writable directories
Serialize any shared queue access
Monitor for duplicate job submission
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate scheduled outputs that ComfyUI may consume as workflow inputs, and ComfyUI’s asynchronous queue can execute them without an explicit verification step. Because neither profile shows a built-in validation boundary, erroneous Airflow outputs can cascade into incorrect image-generation runs. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF ComfyUI consumes Airflow-produced prompts or workflow files directly
IF no human review or schema validation occurs before queueing
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before queue submission
Validate workflow JSON against a schema
Reject jobs missing required metadata
Log and diff generated prompts before execution
requires-engineering: add automated verification of upstream outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are declared for either agent, and both profiles show no requested OAuth scopes or secrets handling. Compliance mismatch is therefore not evidenced. The only plausible issue is operator-chosen data placement, which is a narrow gap rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF operators route regulated data through Airflow into ComfyUI
IF retention or residency policies differ for the same dataset
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document data-class handling rules
Set retention limits on generated artifacts
Review residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated inputs
